text:
Marathon Petroleum ticked up slightly today, but the real story is the 13% surge over two weeks—driven by a sharp jump in oil prices tied to Middle East tensions. Iran has escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and warned of further retaliation if the U.S. strikes again, pushing Brent crude toward $110 a barrel and keeping refiners' input costs elevated. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, so Marathon is running hard while margins remain favorable.

The broader tailwind here is that physical oil delivery costs have ballooned—tanker rates have surged enough that the real cost to move crude is roughly $38 higher per barrel than headline prices suggest. That inflates the value of refined products Marathon sells, even as U.S. crude sits at $101.91. The geopolitical risk premium shows no sign of fading, which supports the refiner's outlook for now.
